I Finally Discovered the Mysterious Western Typeface Used in Old Issues of POPEYE

I finally discovered the typeface I had been searching for since long ago in 2017. Even though it was intermittent, it took me 15 years to find it. However, a year has passed without me having the opportunity to write about it. So, I am writing about it here. This time, that is the story. (It is paid content)
The Western typeface used in old issues of POPEYE

To start with the story of what I had been searching for for such a long time, it is a certain Western typeface that was used in a magazine called POPEYE. POPEYE is a magazine published by Magazine House that is still lined up in convenience stores every month, and I think you have probably seen it at least once.

Please do not jump to the conclusion that I was looking for the font of the POPEYE logo on the cover. That logo was hand-lettered by the genius designer/illustrator Seiichi Horiuchi and is not a general-purpose typeface.

What I was looking for was the Western lettering used for a while in the column corner called "pop*eye" starting from the third issue in 1977. A corner with the same name still exists in the magazine, but the typeface in question is no longer used. So, what kind of typeface was it? I will show you in an illustration.
